title: U.S. House · Florida's 14th District
area: West-central Florida in the Tampa Bay area, including parts of Hillsborough County.

context.text: Florida redrew this district's boundaries in a voluntary mid-decade redistricting ahead of the 2026 elections. Using the district's old lines, Kamala Harris carried the area 53.3%-45.6% in 2024; under the new lines, Donald Trump would have won it 54.7%-44.2%, making it one of 23 Democratic-held districts that Trump carried in 2024. Ballotpedia named this a battleground race; the NRCC named it a target district and the DCCC placed incumbent Kathy Castor in its Frontline program for vulnerable incumbents. As of August 18, 2026, The Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rated the general election Lean Republican, DDHQ/The Hill rated it Lean Democratic, and Sabato's Crystal Ball rated it a Toss-up.
The Democratic primary was canceled and incumbent Kathy Castor advanced unopposed. Mike Beltran won the Republican primary against seven other candidates.

candidates.name: Kathy Castor

summary.text: Kathy Castor is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to Florida's 14th Congressional District, first elected in 2006. An attorney, she previously served on the Hillsborough County Board of Commissioners.

background.text: Born in Miami, Florida in 1966; earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Emory University (1988) and a J.D. from Florida State University College of Law (1991).
Worked as an assistant general counsel for the Florida Department of Community Affairs and as an attorney in private practice.
Served on the Hillsborough County Board of Commissioners from 2002 to 2006 before her election to the U.S. House in 2006.

priorities.text: Campaigning on her tenure in the U.S. House, citing work strengthening the local economy and securing grants and investments for jobs in the Tampa Bay region.
priorities.quote: For nearly two decades, she has delivered for Tampa Bay families by strengthening the local economy, securing grants and investments that create good-paying jobs, and fighting to improve quality of life throughout the region.

priorities.text: Affordable housing: says she is committed to reining in rising housing costs and expanding access to affordable housing.
priorities.quote: Rep. Castor is committed to reining in rising housing costs and expanding access to quality, safe affordable housing.

priorities.text: Jobs and the economy: says she supports Tampa Bay's economic institutions and favors a balanced approach to the federal budget.
priorities.quote: Rep. Castor supports Tampa Bay's economic engines, such as MacDill Air Force Base, Moffitt Cancer Center and the University of South Florida. She believes that a balanced approach for the budget charts a sustainable course for middle-class families

positions.summary: Official issues page describes work in Congress to pass background-check legislation and says she continues to advocate for gun violence prevention.
positions.quote: Throughout her time in Congress, U.S. Rep. Castor has worked to stem the gun violence epidemic in America.

positions.summary: Says she helped draft the Affordable Care Act and has worked against efforts to weaken its patient protections.
positions.quote: She helped to draft the landmark Affordable Care Act that passed in 2010, and she has worked tirelessly against weakening new patient protections, especially for neighbors with pre-existing conditions, and educating neighbors about health insurance enrollment in the new marketplace exchange.

positions.summary: Says the country should be committed to renewable energy and has worked to restore funding for clean-energy initiatives.
positions.quote: Rep. Castor believes that America should be committed to renewable energy and energy conservation, and has fought to restore funding that has been slashed from these initiatives.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Energy and Commerce (Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Communications and Technology; Energy subcommittees) and the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Castor has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions and priorities are drawn from her official House issues pages, which do not currently include text for several other tracked issues (e.g. immigration, tax policy).

candidates.name: Mike Beltran

summary.text: Mike Beltran is the Republican nominee for Florida's 14th Congressional District. A trial attorney and former Florida House member known there as "the Billslayer" for opposing legislation, he is campaigning on the border, taxes, spending, and abortion.

background.text: Attended the University of Pennsylvania and Harvard Law School; moved to Florida and started a business that he still operates.
Served in the Florida House of Representatives from 2018 to 2024, winning election in 2018, 2020 and 2022; did not seek re-election in 2024.
Worked as a trial attorney and litigator at his own firm, Beltran Litigation, P.A., and as an associate at Boies, Schiller & Flexner LLP.

priorities.text: "We need to balance the budget... We also need to complete the wall. Lastly, we should ensure our military is used to protect American interests and our allies bear the cost of defending themselves."
priorities.quote: We need to balance the budget. After decades of profligacy, the interest on accrued debt is now responsible for most of the deficit. We also need to complete the wall. Lastly, we should ensure our military is used to protect American interests and our allies bear the cost of defending themselves.

priorities.text: Campaign website lists securing the border, cutting federal spending, and extending the 2025 "Working Families Tax Cut" (no tax on tips or overtime) among his top platform items.

positions.summary: Voted yes on SB 300, which banned abortion after six weeks of pregnancy (with exceptions for rape, incest, fatal fetal abnormality, and the mother's life).

stated.summary: Says the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision, which returned abortion policy to the states, was correctly decided, with exceptions for rape, incest and the life of the mother.
stated.quote: Mike has always fought to protect life. He believes Dobbs was correctly decided and that states, not Washington bureaucrats, judges, or politicians, should set their own policies that include exceptions for rape, incest, and the life of the mother.

positions.summary: Voted yes on CS/HB 543, which allowed Floridians to carry concealed firearms without a state-issued permit.

stated.summary: Campaign website states he has a "perfect pro-gun record" and opposes red-flag laws and magazine bans.
stated.quote: Mike has a perfect pro-gun record. No red flag laws, no magazine bans, no compromise.

positions.summary: Says he championed school choice in the Florida legislature and would continue that in Washington.
positions.quote: Mike championed school choice in Tallahassee and will bring that fight to Washington.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he stands with President Trump on finishing the border wall and deporting people in the country illegally.
positions.quote: We need to finish the wall, deport the criminals and fraudsters, and restore law and order at our southern border.

record.text: As a Florida state representative, says he voted against several large state entitlement-program expansions targeting housing and medical assistance, saying they resulted in increased costs.
Voted yes on CS/HB 543 (permitless concealed carry of firearms), which passed the Florida House 76-32 on March 24, 2023.
Voted yes on SB 300 (banning abortion after six weeks of pregnancy, with exceptions), which passed the Florida House 70-40 on April 13, 2023.

CS/CS/CS/CS/HB 1 (expanding eligibility for state school-voucher scholarships to all Florida students regardless of income) passed the Florida House 83-27 on March 17, 2023; the official roll call lists Beltran as not voting.

candidates.researchNotes: The record item citing his own self-described votes against entitlement-program expansions (s3) is a paraphrase from his campaign material, not tied to a specific bill/roll-call; it could not be independently verified against an official record.

candidates.name: Brian Lambert

summary.text: Brian Lambert is the Libertarian Party nominee for Florida's 14th Congressional District, advancing from the Libertarian primary without appearing on the ballot. He completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia's coverage confirms Lambert completed a Candidate Connection survey, but his individual Ballotpedia page could not be located under the expected URL in the time available, so his specific survey answers are not included here.

summary.text: Keith Varian is a write-in, no-party-affiliation candidate for Florida's 14th Congressional District. He describes himself as a construction worker and political outsider running against career politicians.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Columbia High School and attended Hudson Valley Community College; works in construction.

priorities.text: Housing affordability, saying it is one of the biggest issues in Florida amid rising costs and hurricane risk.
Controlling federal spending, saying runaway spending and inflation from tariffs are eroding household finances.

positions.summary: Says inflation from tariffs is compounding cost-of-living pressure on working people.
positions.quote: unemployment is on the rise, inflation from tariffs will drown us in a sea of debt.

candidates.name: Salomon Hernandez

summary.text: Salomon Hernandez is a write-in, no-party-affiliation candidate for Florida's 14th Congressional District.

candidates.researchNotes: No Candidate Connection survey, campaign website, or other sourced statement of Hernandez's priorities or positions was found in the time available.
